citations.quote: what is the last innovation that human could ever make?

observation.text: The speaker contrasts the development of humans with animals like tigers and elephants, emphasizing the unique progress of humanity compared to other species.

observation.text: The speaker expresses belief through the repeated use of 'I think' and 'I believe', indicating a personal conviction about AI's impact on jobs.

citations.quote: there is no layoff that has happened so far with this one to one sort of a thing where there was a human doing something suddenly AI came and replaced that work
Any big company if if you speak at this point in time is expecting at least that developer to be thirty percent more productive than the year before.

summary.text: The speaker believes that while there is no direct one-to-one replacement of humans by AI in jobs, AI has started taking over roles by increasing productivity expectations, leading to situations where 30% more productivity is expected without new hires or backfills.

citations.quote: But at least for next two to three years, I don't think the AI will be able to do the things end to end.

summary.text: The speaker believes that front end development will not be dead in the AI era for the next two to three years, as AI will not be capable of handling all development tasks end-to-end in that timeline.
